plain_language: An eleventh AI agent-tool bug landed; the safety default widened to five layers. Fourteen countries now share AI safety checks. A sixth carmaker adopted humanoid robots.
findings:
Friday's cycle closes the second trading week by extending Thursday's four-tier-and-sub-tier signed-load architecture into a five-surface mitigation default in a single business day, pushing the Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter to fourteen named jurisdictions with the first Gulf Cooperation Council formal entry plus a second GCC adjacent track, and adding a sixth OEM-adopted humanoid league-table customer with the first North American 48-hour continuous-operation milestone. Every validation row in today's set scores at the top of the relevance scale except two slightly softer outliers — the disaggregated-prefill substrate-maturity row from May 10 and the capability-attestation defense-prime MSA row from May 11 — and the cross-stream coherence pattern Thursday's summary called out tightens further as one tightly synchronized Friday catalyst stack carries all of the day's high-density axes at once.

On the agentic-AI security axis the tooling-stack CVE wave extends from ten to eleven CVEs at a fresh nested-dependency-resolution surface. Haystack CVE-2026-45013 (CVSS 8.5) drops Friday-morning Pacific as a path-traversal in the pipeline-component manifest fetcher's nested-dependency resolver that lets an attacker overwrite arbitrary host paths during transitive component-manifest resolution, mirroring the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 manifest-fetcher pattern at the nested-dependency-resolution surface; the Haystack maintainer team ships v2.9.4 same-day plus a paired backport advisory for the v2.8.x and v2.7.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Friday extended addendum updating its taxonomy from ten to eleven agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs, reaffirming the four-tier-and-sub-tier signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation plus workflow-state path-canonicalization plus intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization common-mitigation pattern with a nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization extension folded into the manifest-allowlist-validation tier. DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a Friday joint v4 addendum (arxiv 2605.06712v4) extending the runtime-verifier integration pattern to the nested-dependency-resolution sub-tier with Python and Rust reference implementations and formal compositional safety proofs covering all eleven CVE-pattern instances; a fresh standalone Friday paper, Verifiable Nested-Dependency-Resolution Canonicalization for Agentic AI Component-Manifest Loaders (arxiv 2605.07041), provides compositional safety theorems for the extended loader pattern. LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Haystack, and Pydantic AI publish parallel Friday reaffirmation that the mid-June default-shipment commitment now covers all four tier-and-sub-tier surfaces plus the nested-dependency-resolution extension as a paired five-surface delivery — every validation row tied to the framework cohort target (the May 14 mid-June four-surface default prediction, the May 11 framework loader signed-checkpoint plus manifest mode prediction, the May 13 local-LLM workstation three-tier signed-load prediction, the May 12 open-source serving stack signed-checkpoint default prediction, the April 19 indirect-prompt-injection top-CVE-category prediction) lands at the top of the relevance scale.

On the substrate-and-serving axis vLLM v0.11.4-rc2, SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9, and Hugging Face TGI v3.2.2 each ship Friday point releases adding the nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization mitigation as the open-source serving stacks converge ahead of the Monday May 18 vLLM v0.11.4 stable cut; the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh places the shared-prefix workload at approximately 18,940 tok/s on vLLM v0.11.4-rc2 versus 19,460 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9, narrowing the throughput gap to 2.7 percent (from 4.3 percent Thursday) — the tightest gap since the benchmark cycle began — and Cloudflare Infire engineering reports the L40S edge-tier Infire-versus-vLLM ratio holding at parity (1.00x), expected to carry through the Monday stable release. Unsloth's Friday changelog adds an eighth refinement track to the multi-GPU NCCL backend for the router-only LoRA recipe plus extends the intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization primitive to the nested-dependency-resolution pattern: a communication-overlap-optimized tensor-parallel router-attention forward-and-backward pass on octa-Hopper workstation tiers (H100 SXM5 in eight-way NVLink configurations) reporting a further 6 percent training-step time reduction versus Thursday's octa-Hopper mode plus a 4 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on Llama 4 Behemoth router-only training, an extended INT4 ONNX export path now covering the AMD MI350, MI450, and Apple M5 Ultra unified-memory tiers plus the newly-added Qualcomm Cloud AI 100 Ultra inference cohort, plus a community Qwen3.8 30B Mixture-of-Experts recipe at 4 percent peak combined VRAM on dual-RTX 6000 Ada; a sixth Hacker News reproduction lands documenting the Apple Mac Studio 2026 M5 Max workstation completing the Qwen3.8-30B router-only recipe through the new nested-dependency-resolution mitigation at 9 percent peak combined VRAM. Stable Long-Context RL via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition v8 (arxiv 2605.05844v8) ships a Friday extension citing the Unsloth communication-overlap-optimized octa-Hopper kernel plus pre-tested integration with the vLLM v0.11.4-rc2, SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9, and TGI v3.2.2 nested-dependency-resolution-aware loaders simultaneously.

On the policy-and-procurement axis the long-scheduled May 15 14:00 EDT Senate Cyber Subcommittee S-407 classified threshold briefing on the Frontier Model Review Board executive order proceeds on schedule, with the eight-witness slate locked Thursday — NIST Director Locascio, the ODNI cyber lead, the NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director, a Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center representative, the CISA Director, the FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau Chief, and the DOE and Treasury cyber assistant secretaries — testifying in the classified session ahead of a 16:30 EDT unclassified press follow-on. A Friday-evening unclassified summary memo confirms the briefing surfaced no objection to the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway or the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window, and that a classified-annex follow-up question set goes to the witnesses with responses due inside ten business days; the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology confirms its parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft is now circulating for markup scheduling, while White House OSTP holds that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22. The Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter reaches a fresh fourteen-jurisdiction count as Saudi Arabia's National Cybersecurity Authority converts Thursday's adjacent-track pre-commitment into a formal exploratory-observer entry with a 270-day national-consultation window and Qatar's National Cyber Security Agency signals adjacent-track interest as the second GCC member to engage; the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat publishes a Friday-afternoon procedural note confirming the cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema draft Recommendation text is now finalized for formal member-state circulation, with the June 2-6 plenary window unchanged as the operative adoption target, and a fresh Friday companion paper (arxiv 2605.07089) supplies compositional safety theorems for the fourteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field interop against that finalized text. CISA refreshes the KEV catalog entry with a Friday-edition reminder that the May 21 n8n CVE-2026-21858 federal-civilian remediation deadline now sits at T-minus-6 business days, and the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive incorporating the ten-CVE Trail of Bits taxonomy clears the Office of Management and Budget publication queue, scheduled for publication early the following week.

On the production-exposure side Shadowserver day-fifteen n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare) Friday scan extends the post-Monday-spike taper to approximately 2,510 internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances (-16.1 percent from Thursday) with the US cohort at 790 and the India cohort at 425 and the residual long-tail unpatched share falling to 18 percent; Censys honeypot exploitation attempts moderate further to approximately 1.9x baseline at the Friday 09:00 UTC mark (down from Thursday's 2.4x); Microsoft Defender for Cloud, CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne Singularity, and Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR publish a Friday joint follow-on telemetry note adding Gh0st RAT to the C2-framework attribution alongside Thursday's nine frameworks, providing the first four-vendor ten-framework C2 attribution baseline. Sysdig Threat Research reports the median time-from-MCP-server-provisioning to first credential-extraction-attempt on unprotected estates holds at 5 minutes for the fourth consecutive day while Defender-protected tenants extend to approximately 5.4 hours — the gap widens to a 65x ratio (vs 59x Thursday); Wiz Research reports Microsoft Defender for Cloud's MCP-server threat-detection module quarantine rate on net-new MCP servers reaches 45 percent (vs 42 percent Thursday, the fifth consecutive day of expansion); Cisco-Astrix MCP-server identity-gateway tenancy crosses 2,180 enterprise tenants (+12 percent vs Thursday) with Akamai SkyAtlas MCP-firewall at 1,260 tenants; CrowdStrike Falcon for Agentic AI extends the Thursday Amazon Bedrock Agent Registry integration with a Friday Azure AI Foundry Agent Service managed-interop visibility integration, lifting cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane visibility to 91 percent of new MCP-server provisioning events — the first time cross-vendor coverage crosses the 90 percent threshold and the first four-orchestrator managed visibility composition.

On the capital-markets axis Cerebras CBRS prints a fourth consecutive consolidation day to close the second trading week: opening at $197.40, intraday range tightening to $196.30-$199.10, close at $198.60 (up 0.8 percent), trailing-five-session turnover crossing $6.1B, institutional-buyside cumulative net position estimated at 37 percent of float (up from 35 percent Thursday), and a 4.1x call-skew at 14:00 EDT (approximately 71,400 calls versus 17,400 puts — the second-widest call-skew print since the IPO debut session). Bernstein issues a Friday week-close note holding the post-IPO price-target floor at $185 (Market-Perform) and describes the four-consecutive-trading-day consolidation as having fully retired the single-event re-rating characterization in favor of a structural second-week base; Morgan Stanley reiterates a $192 target with the upside-tilt $235 scenario probability lifted to 41 percent (from 38 percent Thursday), Wells Fargo Securities holds Buy at $208, Jefferies reiterates Outperform at $225, and UBS initiates coverage at Neutral with a $205 target as the fifth major desk, bracketing the stock inside a roughly $185-to-$235 analyst band. The SEC Division of Corporation Finance posts a Friday-morning EDGAR release pairing a fourth sample comment letter on AI-services-revenue measurement basis (addressing deferred-revenue recognition timing on multi-year hyperscaler minimum-commit contracts plus segment-disclosure granularity for AI-services-revenue-share pools) with a paired Corp Fin staff observation note on the rev-share-pool earnout-disclosure shape, extending the precedent set anchored by the May 8, May 13, and May 14 sample comment letters; Tenstorrent files a Friday-afternoon substantive response to its Thursday first-round Corp Fin comment letter at the 11-business-day mark of its 30-60 day review window, SambaNova holds the bookrunner roster at six (J.P. Morgan, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo Securities, Barclays Capital, Jefferies as Asia-Pacific co-bookrunner) and confirms the confidential-submission filing target firms to the final week of June, and Groq's Saudi PIF contingent-secondary closure timeline narrows into the 10-21 day window per a Friday Reuters Asia wire. The Mag-7 print-cycle preview cohort (Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research, Jefferies, Goldman Sachs Equity Research) lifts the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability to 87 percent (from 84 percent Thursday) at T-minus-six calendar days to the May 21 Alphabet analyst day, citing both the four-consecutive-trading-day Cerebras consolidation pattern and the Friday Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter as material structural additions, with Morgan Stanley Equity Research joining the cohort jointly expecting Microsoft to ship the AI Services breakout in fiscal Q3 2026 alongside Meta and AWS; Cerebras Engineering confirms a fourth-batch engineering-sample window for late Q3 2026 with AI21 Labs plus Reka AI plus Together AI as the next frontier-and-infrastructure cohort, Nvidia ships fourth-batch Vera Rubin NVL576 engineering samples to Mistral AI plus xAI plus Microsoft Azure, AMD ships first Helios production-rack samples to SoftBank Cloud Japan plus SK Telecom Cloud Korea, Tenstorrent's seventh-wave shipment cadence lifts cumulative racks to 153 against the 280-rack first-half target with a second Latin American sovereign-cloud commitment (Brazil's Magalu Cloud, 2 racks), and AMD Helios plus MI450 commitments cross 10.1GW following a 0.3GW Magalu Cloud and a 0.1GW Saudi Arabia HUMAIN Cloud commitment under the new Gulf cyber-eval reciprocity exploratory-observer framework.

On the physical-AI side Tesla Optimus Gen 3 activates a sixth cohort of 12 units at Fremont, bringing the active count to 72 of the 240-unit production-line allocation (30 percent of full allocation reached) with cycle-time tightening to a 1.04x human-baseline envelope (vs Thursday's 1.06x at the 60-unit milestone), and Tesla Robotics posts a Friday-morning 360-second clip showing the first three-line cross-cell coordination across the Fremont automotive, sub-assembly, and battery-module lines with twenty-eight Optimus Gen 3 units coordinating a multi-station sealed parts-transfer chain — the first three-line coordination demonstration in production. BMW Group's Spartanburg 30-unit Atlas allocation reaches the first North American 48-hour continuous-operation milestone on the assembly-line under-body conveyor task with zero MTBF-impacting incidents; Volkswagen Group's Wolfsburg pilot scales from Thursday's 56 units to 68 units after 72 hours of zero MTBF-impacting incidents and confirms its Optimus cohort first-activation date as June 22, joining BMW Spartanburg as the second OEM running two humanoid platforms in production at one site; Honda Motor Manufacturing Indiana confirms a Friday 30-unit Atlas allocation pilot for fiscal Q3 2026 on the Greensburg vehicle-assembly-line interior-trim sub-assembly task, becoming the sixth OEM-adopted humanoid league-table customer (Tesla, Figure, Apptronik, Boston Dynamics roster, Toyota, Honda) and citing the BMW Spartanburg 48-hour milestone as the operative production-readiness reference; Stellantis confirms its Detroit 60-unit pilot still activates June 8 and reaffirms the Auburn Hills 30-unit second-line pilot for fiscal Q3 2026; and Hyundai Robotics Metaplant Application Center confirms the Atlas humanoid-policy LoRA fine-tune cycle-time improvement on the Dangjin rolling-mill pickup motion stabilizes at 5.1 percent (up from 5.0 percent Thursday — the fourth consecutive day of within-band improvement). On the platform-attestation side Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 day-eight Friday registry telemetry shows 26,180 published skills (+6.3 percent — the fifth consecutive sub-15-percent gain and the second consecutive sub-7-percent reading), 2.49M installs across the eighth 24 hours, and 58 auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills, with Italy's Leonardo Electronics, Germany's Hensoldt Sensors, Norway's Kongsberg Defence Aerospace, and Finland's Patria Land Systems all signing the contractual ethics-and-misuse rider on the Friday business open — lifting the gated cohort to 64 enterprise customers and extending the rider's reach across the Continental European and Nordic allied defense industrial base; Simon Willison's Friday extended note documents that the open-source verification harness now produces a deterministic per-tenant attestation-log audit trail across all 64 gated tenants with cross-tenant compositional safety checks completing in under 58 seconds (improving from Thursday's under-65-second baseline via MIT-CSAIL-contributed parallel-verification optimizations), confirming the lived demonstration cycle holds at three-continent multi-tenant scale.

Dormant-pool reactivations land cleanly on the day's evidence: the Physical AI league tables rank top-five OEM-adopted humanoids prediction (Apr 25) revives on Honda Motor Manufacturing Indiana's Friday 30-unit Atlas commitment becoming the sixth OEM customer plus Tesla's 72-unit Fremont three-line coordination plus BMW Spartanburg's first North American 48-hour continuous-operation milestone plus Volkswagen Wolfsburg's 68-unit scale plus Hyundai Metaplant Dangjin's 5.1 percent improvement; the Agent registry standard converges with MCP for agent artifacts prediction (Apr 19) revives on Mistral's five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix targeting June general availability plus OpenAI's per-org agent registry fourth-wave eight-region Indo-Pacific GA plus CrowdStrike Falcon for Agentic AI's Azure AI Foundry managed-interop integration lifting cross-vendor visibility to 91 percent; and the Indirect prompt injection becomes a top CVE category prediction (Apr 19) revives on Haystack CVE-2026-45013 at the nested-dependency-resolution surface plus the eleven-CVE Trail of Bits taxonomy plus the OMB-publication-queue clearance of the CISA federal-civilian operational directive.
